solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Broadcast trick that can improve the atmosphere?

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A radio stunt that might lighten the mood of listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase for a machine: the question mark flags the play on 'atmosphere' as the air in a room rather than the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircon, short for air conditioning, cools and cleans the air in a room.

clue.text: A run around part of the Circle Line?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
c, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: A dash round a section of the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it means a circle's curved line.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a segment of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: People calling for very close matches

definitions.meaning: first sense: bell-... or those who ring on the phone

explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' reads as contests; it means lookalikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringers are those who ring bells or phones, and a ringer is also a near-identical double.

clue.text: Sort of aerosol from Australia — one kind

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
taken as written
kind means friendly

explanation.surface: A type of spray can of Australian make.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone-friendly aerosols use propellants that do not harm the upper atmosphere's ozone layer.

clue.text: Chemical element from commercial one put in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the commercial and the one are placed inside the drink, so these words signal insertion

parts.note: rum is a spirit
an ad is a commercial
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts: an element derived from an advert and a measure poured into a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Radium is a radioactive metallic element discovered by the Curies.

clue.text: Forfeited rage, resolved to stop arguing?

indicators.note: dissolved and reformed, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Having given up the anger, someone decided to end the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to differ is to drop a dispute while each side keeps its own view.

clue.text: Has no right to hold up golf clubs

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters are read bottom to top
the words contain the answer within them, so these words signal a hidden run of letters

parts.note: the run of letters held across these three words

explanation.surface: Someone lacks the authority to delay a set of golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' picks SNORI out of haS NO RIght; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf clubs with metal heads, numbered by loft.

clue.text: Turbulence in realm most unusual

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Strange disturbances in a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and so any confused, turbulent situation.

clue.text: British party travel to see African river

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A political group takes a trip to view a river in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Congo is the great river of central Africa, second only to the Nile in length on that continent.

clue.text: Elizabethan playwright's horse crossing down

indicators.note: the horse straddles the other word, so it goes around it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: A dramatist's horse walks across a stretch of downland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe wrote Doctor Faustus and was Shakespeare's contemporary.

clue.text: Moon, or half moon, seen above gym

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the second
only the front half of the word is kept, its back half dropped

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class

explanation.surface: The moon or a half moon visible over a gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon' is a verb here: to moon about is to mope.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is to wander about listlessly and dreamily, which is to sulk aimlessly.

clue.text: A person returning in Apocalypse Now

indicators.note: going back, so the letters run right to left
the letters sit within the words of the film title

parts.note: the end of Apocalypse and the start of Now give these letters

explanation.surface: Someone coming back in the Coppola war film Apocalypse Now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ENO from apocalypsE NOw; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: One means a person, as in 'one should always be polite'.

clue.text: Cover ripe bananas, then charge too much

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Wrap ripe bananas, then put a steep price on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit being covered; it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To overprice goods is to set their cost higher than they are worth.

clue.text: Rulers like Victoria, half of them leading forces

indicators.note: the first piece comes in front of the second
only the back half of the word is kept, its front half dropped

parts.note: presses means forces or urges

explanation.surface: Female monarchs such as Victoria, half of whom command armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like military units, but it is a verb: presses.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria was Empress of India, so she was one of a line of female imperial rulers.

clue.text: Guarantee Head avoids criticism

indicators.note: the word's first letter is left out

parts.note: censure is strong criticism

explanation.surface: A promise that the boss escapes being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a boss; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, to guarantee it.

clue.text: Machine in bottling factory? Fine example!

definitions.meaning: first sense: a device that pushes corks into bottles
second sense: an informal word for an excellent specimen

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful coinage for a cork-inserting machine, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A corker is old-fashioned British slang for something outstanding, and literally a thing that corks.

clue.text: Aware of Heart of Darkness: outstanding

indicators.note: only the central letters are taken

parts.note: the middle pair of letters of darkness
a debt outstanding is owing

explanation.surface: Familiar with Conrad's novel Heart of Darkness, which is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' reads as excellent; it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A knowing person is conscious or informed of something.

clue.text: Journey starts on time: on up river

indicators.note: each word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A trip that begins punctually, heading upriver.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'on' just links; the starts of time, on, up, river are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey visiting several places.

clue.text: Spicy food very quietly eaten by eccentric pioneer

indicators.note: placed inside, as food goes into a mouth, so one piece sits within the other
odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An odd frontiersman silently munching something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pioneer' looks like the person doing the eating, but it is only letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spiced Italian-American sausage, a common pizza topping.

clue.text: American writer's visited by small models

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the house, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe's, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A US author's home receives small-scale models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun; it is the verb: poses for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To model is to sit or pose for an artist or photographer.

clue.text: German physicist in love with His Majesty

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A German scientist who has fallen for the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Ohm formulated the law relating voltage, current and resistance.

clue.text: Finally cheer on home team's privileged member?

indicators.note: in an across answer the letter comes after the other pieces

parts.note: being in is being at home
a side is a team; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of cheer

explanation.surface: A fan cheering on the home side at the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means after: the cheer's last letter goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to the inner circle and enjoys access to secret information.

clue.text: Cast's brief relationship

definitions.meaning: first sense: to throw or hurl
second sense: a short-lived romantic affair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors in a play; it is the verb to throw. The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw something, and a fling is a short casual love affair.

clue.text: Grenade primarily a French weapon

indicators.note: first of all, so the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of grenade
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A grenade is chiefly a French arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is a firearm, a weapon that fires bullets.

clue.text: Trials of European, for example, on board steamship

indicators.note: a passenger on board is inside the ship

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: Tests taken by a European passenger on a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt or trial, its original sense.

clue.text: Zero kit fashionable, for a start

parts.note: O looks like zero
rig is equipment or kit
in means trendy

explanation.surface: Smart clothing with nothing on it, worn as a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the beginning or source of something.
